newsitem.title: CHINA: China party elite in annual behind-doors plenum.
newsitem.headline: China party elite in annual behind-doors plenum.

text.p: China's ruling Communist Party central committee and other party elite were gathered behind closed doors in Beijing on Monday for their annual plenum to set policy for the next year, Chinese sources said.
State media made no mention of the annual meeting, which is believed to have started as early as Sunday and usually lasts for about three days.
However, officials have said the meeting would focus on discussing the importance of "spiritual civilisation," communist jargon for values.

Almost two decades of market-oriented economic reform have eroded what Beijing's top leaders regard as orthodox Marxist values, and party chief and state president Jiang Zemin has made clear that he wants to place his stamp on ideology in China.
It was not clear whether any personnel changes in the top echelons of the Politburo, China's most powerful decision-making body, or other party organisations would be announced, Chinese sources said.

Security was tight, with additional police on duty around the site of the meeting in the Jingxi Guesthouse at the western end of Changan Avenue, or the Avenue of Eternal Peace, that cuts through central Beijing.
